clauses.reason: The lead clause says the President does "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved", subject to the conditions that follow. Condition 1 states that "the provisions of this Code shall be in full force and effect only until May 15, 1934", so the approval, a section 3(a) approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Millinery Industry, operated only until that date. The "until" date is recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading (ending when May 15, 1934 begins) is the alternative. S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113, approved June 14, 1935) later repealed the provisions delegating power to approve codes and is a later event; Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.

Condition 1 states that "the provisions of this Code shall be in full force and effect only until May 15, 1934" and that "Prior to that date, the Code Authority shall make recommendations to the Administrator in regard to the continuance or the amendment of any or all provisions of this Code". The code's force ends on May 15, 1934 by the order's own words, and the recommendation direction is tied to the same fixed date and to the continuance of provisions that lapse on it. The "until" date is recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading (ending when May 15, 1934 begins) is the alternative. S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113, approved June 14, 1935) later repealed the provisions delegating power to approve codes and is a later event; Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.

Condition 2 provides that "A special board shall be appointed by the Administrator for the purpose of determining after notice and hearing whether the scales applying to a particular area, market or member of the industry should be stayed or modified because of great and unusual hardship". It is a condition of the approval (section 3(a)) and concerns only the code's wage scales, which applied only until May 15, 1934, so it stopped operating with the approval on that date. No held record shows the board appointed, so no performance date is claimed. The "until" date is recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading (ending when May 15, 1934 begins) is the alternative. S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113, approved June 14, 1935) later repealed the provisions delegating power to approve codes and is a later event; Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.

Condition 3 states that "Provision is made in section 5 of Article IV by which any person on whom undue hardships are imposed may be granted an opportunity for relief". It describes a hardship-relief provision of the code itself and commands nothing further; the provision operated only while the code was in force, until May 15, 1934. The "until" date is recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading (ending when May 15, 1934 begins) is the alternative. S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113, approved June 14, 1935) later repealed the provisions delegating power to approve codes and is a later event; Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6501 is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 373222), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-10-09T17:05:43Z whose heading names Executive Order 6501, whose date (December 15, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1933 Dec 15 p.556: Code of Fair Competition for the Millinery Industry ap proved. IV NRA Codes 1.) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The shared analysis defaults to June 14, 1935, but this order states its own earlier end (condition 1), which is the first end and makes the repeal a later event. The machine inventory (lead approval and conditions 1 to 3) matches the text, so no correction was needed.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition for the Millinery Industry through May 15, 1934 are accrued consequences that the order's own time limit did not turn into continuing commands; nothing held continues the approval after that date, and S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) later repealed the approval and enforcement provisions on June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action while the approval was in effect (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is an accrued effect; the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
